title: How much of a full turn is a right angle?
description: A straight angle is half of a full turn, and it is split into two equal parts, each called a right angle. Half of a half gives one of four equal parts of the full turn. Keeko's doubt is that a right angle is half of a full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: a right angle is half of a straight angle, and a straight angle is half of a full turn, so a right angle is a quarter of a full turn. Watch for students who say a right angle is half a turn.

source: If a straight angle is formed by half of a full turn, how mu
video_script.why: The child finds that a right angle is a quarter of a full turn by halving a half turn.
video_script.substitution: the book's own straight angle split into two right angles, shown against a full turn
video_script.anchor: a full turn drawn as a circle, with the straight angle as half of it and a right angle marked inside
video_script.wrong_answer: a right angle is half of a full turn
video_script.wrong_move: mixes up the right angle with the straight angle
video_script.payoff_line: A right angle is a quarter of a full turn

final_answer.value: 1/4 of a full turn (a quarter turn)
final_answer.spoken: a quarter of a full turn

hold_back: a quarter of a full turn
maths_rules: a straight angle is half of a full turn
a straight angle is split into two equal parts, each a right angle
a right angle is half of a straight angle
half of 1/2 is 1/4, so a right angle is 1/4 of a full turn (a quarter turn)
four right angles make one full turn
slip: a right angle is smaller than the half turn
